Solutions 2 and 3 give the correct answer, d − r. Solution 1's answer of d is wrong.

**Admissibility reduces to containing translates of maximal tori.** A compact A contains a translate of every maximal torus iff it is admissible. For X in some torus T, the orbit exp(ℝX) lies in T, and A is closed, so admissibility forces a translate of T into A. Conversely, a translate of T contains g·exp(tX) for every X in Lie(T).

**Upper bound d − r is attained.** Let n be a lift of a Coxeter element of the Weyl group. Its conjugacy class C has dimension d − r, because n has an r-dimensional centralizer (Kostant). The coset nT₀ lies in C, since n·exp(tY) = exp(tY′)·n-type translates stay in the class. Conjugating gives a translate of every maximal torus inside C. So C is admissible with upper Minkowski dimension d − r.

**Solution 1 fails.** For SU(2), the conjugacy class of j is a 2-sphere, which is admissible by the construction above. Its dimension is 2 < 3 = d, so d cannot be the infimum.

**Lower bound.** Solutions 2 and 3 both argue that the family of maximal tori, which is G/N(T) and has dimension d − r, forces N_δ(A) ≳ δ^{−(d−r)}. Their argument is sketchy, and I did not verify it in full. I am relying on the matching of the upper bound with what I recall as the known result for this problem, which I could not confirm from memory.

Solution 2 is the cleaner write-up of the same correct answer, so I choose it.

CHOICE: 2
